newsitem.title: MEXICO: TFM makes final Mexico rail payment, takes control.
newsitem.headline: TFM makes final Mexico rail payment, takes control.

text.p: Railroad company Transportacion Ferroviaria Mexicana (TFM) took control of Mexico's Northeast Railroad on Monday, after making a final payment of about $800 million to the Mexican government on Sunday.

The first locomotives on the newly privatized railway was sent off bearing the TFM emblem, with President Ernesto Zedillo onlooking along wwith hundreds of rail workers in shiny new uniforms with the TFM logo.
TFM is a joint venture between Mexican transportation company Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) and Kansas City Southern Industries.
In Monterrey TFM set up a customer service center with 113 employees at a construction cost of $800,000, executive vice-president of TFM Brad Skinner told Reuters.

On Dec. 5, TFM won the 50-year concession to operate the railway and own 80 percent of the Northeast railroad with a whopping $1.4 billion bid. The winning bid was almost three times the second largest offer for the line.
The railway connects Nuevo Laredo and Matamoros on the U.S. border with city centers Monterrey, Saltillo and Mexico City and ports Veracruz, Lazaro Cardenas, Altamira and Tampico.
